passage: Step rate was examined in 24 recreational distance runners during overground running across a range of self-selected speeds (3.0–4.5 m·s⁻¹). Associations between step rate and vertical loading rate were investigated using a force-instrumented treadmill.

Ground contact time was measured in 18 novice runners during treadmill running at imposed speeds of 2.5, 3.5, and 4.5 m·s⁻¹. The relationship between contact time and tibial acceleration was examined across the imposed speed conditions.

Aerial time was assessed in 22 distance runners during overground running using high-speed motion capture. Associations between flight time and preferred running speed were examined in both male and female participants.

The proportion of stride time spent in contact with the ground was measured in 16 recreational runners during treadmill running at self-selected pace. The relationship between duty factor and ground reaction force magnitude was investigated using force plate data.

Stride length was quantified in 28 novice runners during overground running at a constant speed of 3.5 m·s⁻¹ using motion capture. Associations between stride length and hip joint loading were examined in a cohort of female recreational runners.

Vertical center of mass displacement was measured in 20 distance runners during treadmill running at speeds ranging from 2.8 to 5.0 m·s⁻¹ using motion analysis. The relationship between vertical oscillation and injury history was examined in a prospective study of recreational runners.

The ratio of vertical center of mass oscillation to step length was calculated in 24 recreational runners during overground running at self-selected speeds. Associations between vertical ratio and metabolic cost were examined using indirect calorimetry.

Foot strike position relative to center of mass was analyzed in 19 distance runners during treadmill running at 3.5 m·s⁻¹ using video analysis. The relationship between foot placement anterior to body center of mass and peak braking force was examined across trained and novice runners.

Foot contact angle was quantified in 26 recreational runners during overground running using high-speed video and marker tracking. Associations between foot strike angle and tibial acceleration were examined in runners with and without a history of stress fracture.

Sagittal plane knee flexion at initial contact was measured in 21 distance runners during treadmill running at speeds of 3.0, 3.8, and 4.5 m·s⁻¹ using three-dimensional motion capture. The relationship between knee flexion angle at contact and knee joint loading was examined using inverse dynamics.

Trunk inclination angle was quantified in 23 recreational runners during overground running using marker-based motion capture at a constant speed of 3.5 m·s⁻¹. Associations between forward trunk lean and ground reaction force magnitude were examined across male and female participants.
